query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Changing the percentage of elements in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA alters its mechanical properties due to variations in lattice distortion and atomic interactions.
generation.intervention: Varying the percentage of elements (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) in the alloy
generation.mechanism: Changes in lattice distortion and atomic interactions affect the alloy's mechanical behavior
generation.predicted_outcome: Altered mechanical properties (e.g., strength, ductility, hardness) in response to changes in elemental composition
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties of the initial HfNbTaTiZr-HEA composition
generation.boundary: Limits of elemental composition variations that retain the alloy's high-entropy characteristics
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient data on the specific effects of individual elemental variations on mechanical properties

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of elemental composition in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA, followed by mechanical property characterization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant changes in mechanical properties are observed with variations in elemental composition, the hypothesis is falsified
